# Toronto University Library

### Presented by

->The British and Foreign Bible Society <note>Founded in 1804, this non-denominational society aimed to provide Bibles in various languages and at affordable prices across the globe.</note><-
->through the Committee formed in<-
->The Old Country <note>A term used by settlers and residents in Canada and other colonies to refer to the United Kingdom or Great Britain.</note><-
->to aid in replacing the loss caused by<-
->The disastrous Fire of February the 14th 1890 <note>On Valentine's Day in 1890, a kerosene lamp was knocked over in the eastern wing of University College, resulting in a fire that consumed over 30,000 volumes—nearly the entire library collection at the time.</note><-

<summary>This document is a formal dedication label from a book donated by the British and Foreign Bible Society to help rebuild the Toronto University Library collection after it was destroyed by fire in 1890.</summary>

## Chapter One to Chapter 2, Verse 3

<margin>1-2</margin> In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. * And the earth was *waste and void*, and upon the
<margin>3</margin> face of the deep was darkness. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters. * And God said, "Let there be light," and there was
<margin>4-5</margin> light. * And God saw the light, that it was good. And God divided the light from the darkness. * And God called the
light Day, and the darkness He called Night. And there was evening and there was morning, one day.
<margin>6-7</margin> And God said, "Let there be a <term>firmament</term> <note>Arabic: *jalad*. Historically understood as a solid dome or vast expanse that separates the celestial waters from the terrestrial ones.</note> in the midst of the waters, and let it be a divider between waters and waters." * And God
made the firmament and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament. And it was
<margin>8</margin> so. * And God called the firmament Heaven. And there was evening and there was morning, a second day.
<margin>9</margin> And God said, "Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together into one place, and let the dry land appear." And it was
<margin>10</margin> so. * And God called the dry land Earth, and the gathering of the waters He called Seas. And God saw that
<margin>11</margin> it was good. * And God said, "Let the earth sprout grass and herbs yielding seed, and fruit trees bearing
<margin>12</margin> fruit after their kind, whose seed is in it, upon the earth." And it was so. * And the earth brought forth grass
and herbs yielding seed after their kind, and trees bearing fruit, whose seed is in it, after their kind. And God saw that it was
<margin>13</margin> good. * And there was evening and there was morning, a third day.
<margin>14</margin> And God said, "Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be
<margin>15</margin> for signs, and seasons, and days, and years. * And let them be for lights in the firmament of heaven to give light upon the earth."
<margin>16</margin> And it was so. * And God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day and the
<margin>17</margin> lesser light to rule the night, and the stars. * And God set them in the firmament of heaven to give light upon the earth,
<margin>18</margin> * and to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was
<margin>19</margin> good. * And there was evening and there was morning, a fourth day.
<margin>20</margin> And God said, "Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth..."

## Chapter Three

1 Now the serpent was more cunning <term>cunning</term> <note>Arabic: *ahayl*. This term implies being more clever, shrewd, or deceptive than any other living creature.</note> than all the wild animals that the Lord God <term>Lord God</term> <note>Arabic: *al-Rabb al-Ilah*. This title combines the personal name of God (represented by Lord) with the general term for Deity.</note> had made. 
2 And he said to the woman, "Did God truly say, 'You shall not eat from every tree of the garden'?" * And the woman said to the serpent,
3 "We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden; * but of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God has said, 'You shall not
4–5 eat of it, nor shall you touch it, lest you die.'" * Then the serpent said to the woman, "You will not surely die. * For God knows
6 that in the day you eat of it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil." * So when the
woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and a tree desirable to look upon,
7 she took of its fruit and ate. She also gave to her husband with her, and he ate. * Then the eyes of both
of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together and made themselves loincloths.
8 And they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the garden at the blowing of the wind of the day <note>original: *hubub rih al-nahar*. Traditionally translated as "the cool of the day," this refers to the time in the late afternoon when a breeze usually begins to blow.</note>. So Adam
9 and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the Lord God among the trees of the garden. * Then the Lord God called to

12 of which I commanded you that you should not eat?" * Then Adam said, "The woman whom You gave to be with me, she
13 gave me of the tree, and I ate." * And the Lord God said to the woman, "What is this that you have done?" 
14 The woman said, "The serpent deceived me, and I ate." * So the Lord God said to the serpent: "Because you have done
this, you are cursed more than all cattle, and more than every beast of the field; on your belly
15 you shall go, and you shall eat dust all the days of your life. * And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between
16 your offspring and her offspring; He shall crush your head, and you shall crush His heel." * To the woman He said, "I will greatly
multiply your sorrow in your conception; in pain you shall bring forth children; and your desire shall be for your husband, and he
17 shall rule over you." * Then to Adam He said, "Because you have heeded the voice of your wife, and have eaten from the tree
of which I commanded you, saying, 'You shall not eat of it': Cursed is the ground because of you; in toil you shall eat of it

## Chapter Twenty-Six

<margin>1</margin> Now there was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. And in your descendants all the nations of the earth shall be blessed, <margin>5</margin> because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws." <margin>6</margin> So Isaac stayed in Gerar.

<margin>7</margin> When the men of the place asked about his wife, he said, "She is my sister," for he was afraid to say "My wife," thinking, "Lest the men of the place kill me on account of Rebekah, because she was beautiful to look upon." <margin>8</margin> And it happened, when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech, king of the Philistines, looked out of a window <margin>9</margin> and saw, and behold, Isaac was <note>original: "yulā‘ibu"; a word meaning playing or caressing, indicating an intimacy that revealed they were husband and wife.</note> sporting with Rebekah his wife. <margin>12</margin> Isaac sowed in that land and reaped in the same year a hundredfold, and the Lord blessed him. <margin>13</margin> The man became great and continued to prosper until he became very wealthy. <margin>14</margin> He had possessions of flocks and herds and many servants, so the Philistines envied him. <margin>15</margin> And all the wells which his father’s servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines stopped them up and filled them with earth.

## Chapter Thirty-Three

## Chapter Ten

1 Then the Lord said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his servants, that I might perform these signs of Mine among them, 
2 and that you may tell in the hearing of your son and your son’s son what I have done in Egypt and My signs which I have performed among them, that you may know that I am the Lord." 
3 So Moses and Aaron came in to Pharaoh and said to him, "Thus says the Lord God of the Hebrews <term>العبرانيين</term>: How long will you refuse to humble yourself before Me? Let My people go, that they may worship Me. 
4 For if you refuse to let My people go, behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts <term>جراد</term> into your borders <note>original: "تخومك" — referring to the territories or boundaries of the land</note>. 
5 And they shall cover the face of the earth, so that no one will be able to see the earth; and they shall eat the residue of what has escaped, which remains to you from the hail, and they shall eat every tree which grows for you out of the field. 
6 They shall fill your houses, the houses of all your servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians—which neither your fathers nor your fathers’ fathers have seen, since the day that they were on the earth to this day." Then he turned and went out from the presence of Pharaoh.
7 Then Pharaoh’s servants said to him, "How long shall this man be a snare to us? Let the men go, that they may worship the Lord their God. Do you not yet know that Egypt is destroyed?" 
8 So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, and he said to them, "Go, worship the Lord your God. But who and who are the ones going?" 
9 And Moses said, "We will go with our young and our old; with our sons and our daughters, with our flocks and our herds we will go, for we must hold a feast to the Lord." 
10 Then he said to them, "The Lord be with you if I ever let you and your little ones go! Look, evil is before your faces. 
11 Not so! Go now, you who are men, and worship the Lord, for that is what you were seeking." And they were driven out from Pharaoh’s presence.

<margin>20</margin> in all the territories of Egypt. But the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not let the Children of Israel go.

<margin>22</margin> be felt." So Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and there was thick darkness in all the land of Egypt 
<margin>23</margin> for three days. They did not see one another, nor did anyone rise from his place for three days. But all the Children of Israel had light in their dwellings.

# Leviticus

## Chapter One

<margin>1-2</margin> And the Lord called Moses and spoke to him from the **Tent of Meeting** <note>original: "khaymat al-ijtima'" – the portable sanctuary where God met with His people</note>, saying: * Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: If a man among you brings an <term>offering</term> <note>original: "qurban" – a gift or sacrifice brought near to God</note> to the Lord of the livestock, you shall bring your offerings from the cattle and the sheep.
<margin>3</margin> * If his offering is a <term>burnt offering</term> <note>original: "muhraqa" – an offering entirely consumed by fire, symbolizing total devotion</note> from the cattle, he shall offer a male without blemish. He shall present it at the door of the Tent of 
<margin>4</margin> Meeting so that he may be accepted before the Lord. * And he shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it shall be accepted 
<margin>5</margin> for him to make <term>atonement</term> <note>original: "takfir" – the act of making amends or covering sin</note> for him. * And he shall slaughter the calf before the Lord, and the sons of Aaron the priests shall bring the blood 
<margin>6</margin> and sprinkle the blood all around on the altar that is by the door of the Tent of Meeting. * And he shall skin 
<margin>7</margin> the burnt offering and cut it into its pieces. * And the sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar and arrange 
<margin>8</margin> wood on the fire. * And the sons of Aaron the priests shall arrange the pieces, along with the head and the fat, over 
<margin>9</margin> the wood that is on the fire which is on the altar. * But its entrails and its legs he shall wash with water, and the priest shall burn the whole on the altar as a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to the Lord.
<margin>10</margin> * And if his offering is from the flock—from the sheep or the goats—as a burnt offering, he shall offer a male without blemish. 
<margin>11</margin> * And he shall slaughter it on the side of the altar to the north before the Lord. And the sons of Aaron the priests shall sprinkle 
<margin>12</margin> its blood on the altar all around. * And he shall cut it into its pieces, with its head and its fat, and the priest shall arrange them 
<margin>13</margin> over the wood that is on the fire which is on the altar. * But the entrails and the legs he shall wash with water, and the priest shall bring everything and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to the Lord.
<margin>14</margin> * And if his offering to the Lord is a burnt offering of birds, then he shall bring his offering of turtledoves or of young 
<margin>15</margin> pigeons. * The priest shall bring it to the altar, wring off its head, and burn it on the altar; and its blood shall be drained out on the 
<margin>16</margin> wall of the altar. * And he shall remove its crop with its feathers and cast it beside the altar on the east, to the place of 
<margin>17</margin> the ashes. * And he shall split it open by its wings, but shall not divide it. And the priest shall burn it on the altar over the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to the Lord.

<summary>This page marks the beginning of Leviticus, providing specific instructions for the burnt offering (Olah). It details the different types of animals allowed—cattle, sheep, goats, or birds—and the precise rituals the priests must perform to ensure the sacrifice is a "sweet aroma" to God.</summary>

## Chapter Two

<margin>1</margin> And when anyone brings an offering of a **grain offering** <term>grain offering</term> <note>original: "taqdimah" – a tribute of fine flour and oil, representing the gift of one's daily sustenance to God</note> to the Lord, his offering shall be of fine flour. And he shall pour
<margin>2</margin> oil on it and put **frankincense** <note>original: "luban" – a precious aromatic resin used in sacred incense</note> on it. * And he shall bring it to the sons of Aaron, the priests, and he shall take from it a handful of its fine flour and its oil, with all its frankincense, and the priest shall burn its **memorial portion** <note>original: "tadhkar" – the representative portion burned on the altar to bring the worshiper to God's "mind"</note> on the altar, a fire offering of a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
<margin>3</margin> * And the remainder of the grain offering is for Aaron and his sons. It is a **Most Holy** <term>Most Holy</term> <note>original: "quds aqdas" – items that were especially sacred and could only be eaten by the priests within the sanctuary</note> portion from the fire offerings of the Lord.
<margin>4</margin> And if you bring an offering of a grain offering baked in an oven, it shall be unleavened cakes of fine flour
<margin>5</margin> mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil. * And if your offering is a grain offering on a **griddle** <note>original: "al-saj" – a flat metal plate for baking</note>,
<margin>6</margin> it shall be of fine flour, unleavened, mixed with oil. * You shall break it into pieces and pour oil on it. It is a grain offering.
<margin>7-8</margin> And if your offering is a grain offering from a **pan**, it shall be made of fine flour with oil. * And you shall bring the grain offering
<margin>9</margin> that is made of these things to the Lord and present it to the priest, and he shall bring it near the altar. * And the priest shall take
<margin>10</margin> from the grain offering its memorial portion and burn it on the altar, a fire offering of a pleasing aroma to the Lord. * And the remainder of the grain offering is for Aaron and his sons, a Most Holy portion from the fire offerings of the Lord.
<margin>11</margin> No grain offering that you bring to the Lord shall be made with **leaven** <note>original: "khamir" – yeast or sourdough; its exclusion often symbolized purity and haste</note>. For you shall burn no leaven nor any
<margin>12</margin> **honey** <note>original: "asal" – likely referring to fruit nectar or bee honey, which, like leaven, can ferment</note> as a fire offering to the Lord. * As an offering of **firstfruits** <term>firstfruits</term> <note>original: "awail" – the very first harvest of the season</note> you may bring them to the Lord, but
<margin>13</margin> they shall not be offered on the altar for a pleasing aroma. * And you shall season every grain offering with salt, and you shall not let the **salt of the covenant** of your God be missing from your grain offering. With all your offerings you shall offer salt.
<margin>14</margin> And if you bring a grain offering of firstfruits to the Lord, you shall bring crushed heads of new grain roasted in the fire, ground into grits, as the
<margin>15</margin> <margin>16</margin> grain offering of your firstfruits. * And you shall put oil on it and lay frankincense on it. It is a grain offering. * And the priest shall burn its memorial portion from its grits and its oil, with all its frankincense, as a fire offering to the Lord.

<margin>3</margin> and the sons of Aaron the priests shall sprinkle the blood all around on the altar. * And he shall offer from the peace offering as a fire offering to the Lord the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails.

<margin>29</margin> and if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, it shall be scoured and rinsed with water. Every male among the priests may eat of it;
<margin>30</margin> it is **most holy**. But no sin offering from which any of the blood is brought into the tent of meeting
to make atonement in the Holy Place shall be eaten; it shall be burned with fire.'"

### Chapter Seven

<margin>1-2</margin> And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: "Take Aaron and his sons with him, and the garments, the **anointing oil** <note>original: "dehn al-mas'ha" — a sacred oil used to consecrate people and objects for God's service</note>, the bull of the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.

<margin>7</margin> And he put the tunic on him, girded him with the sash, clothed him with the robe, and put the **ephod** <note>original: "al-rida'" — a ceremonial vest-like garment worn by the High Priest</note> on him. <margin>13</margin> Then Moses brought Aaron’s sons and clothed them in tunics, girded them with sashes, and fastened **caps** <note>original: "qalans" — head coverings or turbans for the ordinary priests</note> on them, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

<margin>16</margin> Then he poured the blood at the base of the altar and consecrated it to make atonement for it. He took all the fat that was on the entrails, the fatty lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and Moses burned them on the altar.

<margin>19</margin> He slaughtered it, and Moses sprinkled the blood on the altar all around.
<margin>20</margin> He cut the ram into pieces, and Moses burned the head, the pieces, and the fat.
<margin>21</margin> Then he washed the entrails and the legs with water, and Moses burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering for a **pleasing aroma** <note>original: "rai'hat surur" — a metaphorical expression meaning the offering was accepted by God</note>, an offering made by fire to the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

## Chapter Twenty-Three

<margin>1-2</margin> And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, * Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: The appointed feasts of the Lord, in which
<margin>3</margin> you shall proclaim sacred assemblies <note>original: "محافل مقدسة" (mahafil muqaddasa); these are times when the community is called together for worship.</note>, these are my appointed feasts. * Six days shall work be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of solemn rest, a sacred assembly. You shall do no work; it is a Sabbath to the Lord in all your dwellings.

<margin>4-5</margin> These are the appointed feasts of the Lord, the sacred assemblies which you shall proclaim at their appointed times. * In the
<margin>6</margin> first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at twilight <note>original: "بين العشاءين" (bayn al-'isha'ayn), literally "between the two evenings," the time between sunset and total darkness.</note>, is the Lord’s Passover. * And on the fifteenth day
<margin>7</margin> of this month is the Feast of Unleavened Bread to the Lord; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. * On the first day you shall have
<margin>8</margin> a sacred assembly; you shall do no customary work. * And for seven days you shall present an offering by fire to the Lord. On the seventh day is a sacred assembly; you shall do no customary work.

<margin>9-10</margin> And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, * Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land which I give to you and reap its harvest, then you shall bring the sheaf <note>original: "حزمة" (huzma); refers to the 'Omer,' the first measurement of the grain harvest.</note> of the firstfruits of your harvest to the priest.
<margin>11</margin> * He shall wave the sheaf <term>wave offering: a ritual where the priest moves the offering in specific directions to symbolize presenting it to God</term> before the Lord, to be accepted on your behalf; on the day after the Sabbath the priest shall wave it. * And you shall offer
<margin>12</margin> on that day when you wave the sheaf, a male lamb of the first year without blemish as a burnt offering to the Lord. * Its grain
<margin>13</margin> offering shall be two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering by fire to the Lord for a soothing aroma; and its drink offering shall be of wine, one-fourth of a hin <note>A "hin" is an ancient liquid measure, roughly 4 liters; a quarter hin is about 1 liter.</note>.
<margin>14</margin> * You shall eat neither bread nor parched grain nor fresh ears <note>original: "فريكاً وسويقاً" (farikan wa sawiqan); different preparations of new grain.</note> until this selfsame day, until you have brought the offering of your God; it shall be a statute forever throughout your generations in all your dwellings.

<margin>15</margin> And you shall count for yourselves from the day after the Sabbath, from the day that you brought the sheaf of the wave offering: seven full weeks
<margin>16</margin> shall be completed. * Count fifty days to the day after the seventh Sabbath; then you shall offer a new grain
<margin>17</margin> offering to the Lord. * You shall bring from your dwellings two wave loaves of two-tenths of an ephah; they shall be of fine
<margin>18</margin> flour; they shall be baked with leaven as firstfruits to the Lord. * And you shall offer with the bread seven lambs of the first year without blemish, one young bull, and two rams. They shall be a burnt offering to the Lord, with their grain offering and their drink offerings, an offering by fire for a soothing
<margin>19</margin> aroma to the Lord. * Then you shall sacrifice one kid of the goats as a sin offering, and two male lambs of the first year as
<margin>20</margin> a sacrifice of peace offering. * The priest shall wave them with the bread of the firstfruits as a wave offering before the Lord, with the two lambs.

<margin>1-2</margin> And the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying: * Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When

seventh month; on the tenth day of the month, on the Day of Atonement, you shall sound the trumpet throughout all your land. * And you shall 
<margin>10</margin> consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty <note>original: "عتق" ('itq); meaning liberation or manumission, particularly for those in debt-servitude.</note> in the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee <term>Jubilee [Yubil]: A sacred year occurring every 50 years when debts were forgiven and ancestral lands were returned to their original owners.</term> for you, 
<margin>11</margin> and each of you shall return to his possession, and each of you shall return to his family. * The fiftieth year shall be a jubilee 
for you; you shall not sow, nor reap its voluntary growth, nor gather from its untended vines. * For it is a jubilee; 
<margin>12</margin> it shall be holy to you. You shall eat its produce from the field. * In this Year of Jubilee, each of you shall return 
<margin>13</margin> to his possession. * And when you sell anything to your neighbor or buy from your neighbor's hand, 
<margin>14</margin> you shall not wrong one another.

**3** ...to make the vow of a Nazirite <term>Nazirite: from the Hebrew word 'nazir', meaning 'consecrated' or 'separated'</term>, to separate himself to the Lord. * He shall separate himself from wine and strong drink; he shall drink no vinegar of wine nor

**4** vinegar of strong drink; neither shall he drink any grape juice, nor eat fresh grapes or dried raisins. * All the days of his vow

**5** he shall eat nothing that is produced by the grapevine, from the seeds even to the skin. * All the days of the vow of his separation, no razor <note>original: "موسى" (mūsā) is spelled the same as the name 'Moses', but here refers to a razor</note> shall pass over his head. Until the completion of the days for which he separates himself to the Lord, he shall be

**6** holy, and he shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow long. * All the days of his separation to the Lord, he shall not go near a dead body.

**7** * Even for his father, his mother, his brother, or his sister, he shall not make himself unclean <note>Ritual impurity caused by contact with death</note> at their death, because the consecration of his God is upon his head.

**8-9** * All the days of his separation he is holy to the Lord. * And if anyone dies very suddenly beside him,

**10** and he defiles his consecrated head, then he shall shave his head on the day of his cleansing; on the seventh day he shall shave it. * And on the

**11** eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest, to the door of the tabernacle of meeting <term>tabernacle of meeting: the portable tent-sanctuary used by the Israelites</term>.

**12** * The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and make atonement for him because he sinned by reason of the dead body. He shall consecrate his head that same day. * When he separates to the Lord the days of his separation, he shall bring a male lamb

**13** in its first year as a guilt offering; but the former days shall be lost, because his separation was defiled. * And this is the law of the Nazirite: when the days of his separation are fulfilled, he shall be brought to the door of the tabernacle of meeting.

**14** * And he shall present his offering to the Lord: one male lamb a year old without blemish as a burnt offering, and one ewe lamb a year old

**15** without blemish as a sin offering, and one ram without blemish as a peace offering, * and a basket of unleavened bread, cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, with their grain offering and their drink offerings.

**16-17** * The priest shall present them before the Lord and offer his sin offering and his burnt offering. * And he shall offer the ram

**18** as a peace offering to the Lord, with the basket of unleavened bread; the priest shall also offer its grain offering and its drink offering. * Then the Nazirite shall shave his consecrated head at the door of the tabernacle of meeting, and shall take the hair of his consecrated head and put it

**19** on the fire which is under the sacrifice of the peace offering. * And the priest shall take the boiled shoulder of the ram, and one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and shall put them upon the hands of the Nazirite after he has shaved

**20** his consecrated hair. * And the priest shall wave them as a wave offering <note>a ritual where the offering is moved back and forth before the altar</note> before the Lord; they are holy for the priest, together with the breast of the wave offering

**21** and the thigh of the heave offering. After that the Nazirite may drink wine. * This is the law of the Nazirite who makes a vow.

<note>Vocabulary used in the text: The Nazirite, The Lord, wine, sacrifice, tabernacle of meeting, yearling, unleavened bread, ram, offering.</note>

"Speak to the children of Israel, that they bring to you a red heifer <term>red heifer: "بقرة حمراء" (baqara hamra'), a rare cow used in a specific ritual to produce ashes for ritual purification.</term>, healthy and without defect, and upon which no <margin>3</margin> yoke has ever been placed. You shall give it to Eleazar the priest, and it shall be taken outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence. <margin>4</margin> Eleazar the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and sprinkle it toward the front of the Tent of <margin>5</margin> Meeting seven times. Then the heifer shall be burned in his sight; its hide, its flesh, and its blood, <margin>6</margin> along with its offal, shall be burned. The priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop <term>hyssop: "زوفا" (zufa), a small aromatic plant used in biblical times for sprinkling during purification rites.</term>, and scarlet yarn, and throw them into the midst of the burning <margin>7</margin> heifer. Then the priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; afterward, he may enter the camp, <margin>8</margin> but the priest shall be unclean until evening. The one who burned it shall also wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water, and shall be unclean until evening. <margin>9</margin> A man who is clean shall gather the ashes of the heifer and place them outside the camp in a clean place. They shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Israel for the preparation of the water of impurity <note>original: "ماء نجاسة" (ma' najasa). This refers to the water mixed with the heifer's ashes, used specifically to cleanse those who have become ritually "unclean."</note>. <margin>10</margin> It is a sin offering. The one who gathered the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. This shall be a perpetual statute for the children of Israel and for the stranger who dwells among them.

<margin>11</margin> Whoever touches the corpse of any human being shall be unclean for seven days. He must purify himself with [the water] on the third day, and on the seventh day he shall be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third day, then on the <margin>13</margin> seventh day he will not be clean. Whoever touches a corpse—the body of a person who has died—and does not purify himself, defiles the Tabernacle of the Lord. That soul shall be cut off from Israel <note>To be "cut off" usually implied excommunication from the community or divine punishment.</note>. Because the water of impurity was not sprinkled on him, he remains unclean; his uncleanness is still upon him.

<margin>14</margin> This is the law: When a person dies in a tent, everyone who enters the tent and everyone <margin>15</margin> who was in the tent shall be unclean for seven days. Every open vessel that does not have a lid <margin>16</margin> fastened with a band is unclean. Also, whoever in the open field touches one who was killed by a sword, or a corpse, or a human bone, or a grave, shall be unclean for seven days. <margin>17</margin> For the unclean person, they shall take some of the ashes of the burned sin offering and pour living water <term>living water: "ماء حي" (ma' hayy), meaning fresh, flowing water from a spring or stream, rather than stagnant water.</term> over them in a vessel. <margin>18</margin> A clean man shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the furnishings, on the people who were there, and on the one who touched the bone, the slain, the corpse, or the grave. <margin>19</margin> The clean person shall sprinkle the unclean on the third day and on the seventh day, and purify him on the [seventh] day..."

<margin>2</margin> And they stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and all the congregation at the door of the Tabernacle of <margin>3</margin> Meeting, saying: "Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the people who gathered against the Lord in the company of Korah <note>Korah led a famous rebellion against Moses' authority; those involved were barred from inheritance. See Numbers 16.</note>, but he died for his own sin and had no sons. <margin>4</margin> Why should the name of our father be removed from among his clan because he has no son? Give us a possession <note>original Arabic: *milkan*, referring here to a land holding or estate</note> among our father’s brothers."

<margin>5</margin> So Moses presented their case before the Lord.

<margin>6-7</margin> And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: "The daughters of Zelophehad speak righteously. You shall surely give them a possession of <margin>8</margin> inheritance among their father’s brothers, and cause the inheritance of their father to pass to them. And you shall speak to the children of Israel, <margin>9</margin> saying: 'If a man dies and has no son, then you shall cause his inheritance to pass to his daughter. <margin>10</margin> If he has no daughter, then you shall give his inheritance to his brothers. If he has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to his father’s brothers. <margin>11</margin> And if his father has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to his next of kin, the closest to him in his clan, and he shall possess it.'" This became a statute of judgment <term>statute of judgment: *faridat qada'*, a permanent legal decree</term> for the children of Israel, just as the Lord commanded Moses.

<margin>12</margin> And the Lord said to Moses: "Go up into this Mount Abarim <note>A mountain range across from Jericho, providing a view of the Land of Canaan.</note> and see the land which I have given to <margin>13</margin> the children of Israel. When you have seen it, you also shall be gathered to your people <note>A biblical idiom for death and joining one's ancestors.</note>, just as Aaron your brother was gathered. <margin>14</margin> For in the Wilderness of Zin, during the strife of the congregation, you both rebelled against My command to hallow Me at the waters before their eyes." (These are the waters of Meribah <note>original Arabic: *Ma' Muribah*, meaning "Waters of Strife."</note> in Kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin.)

<margin>15</margin> Then Moses spoke to the Lord, <margin>16</margin> saying: "Let the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation, <margin>17</margin> who may go out before them and go in before them, who may lead them out and bring them in, so that the congregation of the Lord may not be like sheep which have no shepherd."

<margin>18</margin> And the Lord said to Moses: "Take Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand upon him. <margin>19</margin> Set him before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation, and inaugurate him in their sight. <margin>20</margin> And give some of your authority <note>original Arabic: *haybatika*, meaning your majesty or awe-inspiring presence</note> to him, so that all the congregation of the children of Israel may be obedient. <margin>21</margin> He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall inquire for him by the judgment of the Urim <term>Urim: sacred lots used by the High Priest to determine God's will</term> before the Lord. At his word they shall go out, and at his word they shall come in, both he and all the children of Israel with him, all the congregation."

<margin>22</margin> And Moses did as the Lord commanded him. He took Joshua and set him before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation. <margin>23</margin> He laid his hands on him and inaugurated him, just as the Lord had spoken by the hand of Moses.

## Chapter Twenty-Eight

<margin>1-2</margin> And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: "Command the children of Israel and say to them: 'My offering, My food for My fire offerings <note>original: *waqa'idi*, referring to sacrifices consumed by fire</note>, a soothing aroma <note>Arabic: *ra’ihat sururi*, literally "aroma of my joy/pleasure"</note>, you shall be careful to offer to Me at its appointed time.' <margin>3</margin> And say to them: 'This is the fire offering that you shall offer to the Lord: two yearling lambs without blemish for each day as a continual burnt offering. <margin>4-5</margin> One lamb you shall prepare in the morning, and the second lamb you shall prepare between the two evenings <note>The period between sunset and total darkness</note>. And a tenth of an ephah <term>Ephah: a standard biblical dry measure, approximately 22 liters</term> of fine flour mixed <note>original: *maltut*, meaning kneaded or saturated with oil</note> with a quarter of a hin <term>Hin: a liquid measure, approximately 3.6 liters</term> of pressed oil as a grain offering. <margin>6</margin> It is a continual burnt offering, the kind made at Mount Sinai, as a soothing aroma, a fire offering to the Lord. <margin>7</margin> And its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin for each lamb; in the sanctuary, you shall pour out a drink offering of strong wine <note>original: *maskar*, referring to fermented or strong drink</note> to the Lord. <margin>8</margin> And the second lamb you shall prepare between the two evenings; like the morning grain offering and its drink offering, you shall prepare it as a fire offering of a soothing aroma to the Lord. <margin>9</margin> And on the Sabbath day, two yearling lambs without blemish, and two-tenths of fine flour mixed <margin>10</margin> with oil as a grain offering with its drink offering. This is the burnt offering of every Sabbath, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.'

<margin>11</margin> 'And at the beginnings of your months <note>Referring to the New Moon festivals</note>, you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord: two young bulls, one ram, and <margin>12</margin> seven yearling lambs without blemish. And three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering <margin>13</margin> for each bull, and two-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for the one ram. And one-tenth of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for each lamb; it is a burnt offering of a soothing aroma, a fire offering <margin>14</margin> to the Lord. This is the burnt offering of every month throughout the months of the year. And one male goat from the goats shall be offered as a sin offering to the Lord; it shall be offered in addition to the continual burnt offering with its drink offering.'

<margin>16</margin> 'And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is the Lord’s Passover. <margin>17</margin> And on the fifteenth day of this month is a feast; for seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten. <margin>18-19</margin> On the first day there shall be a holy convocation; you shall do no customary work. And you shall offer a fire offering as a burnt offering to the Lord: two young bulls, one ram, and seven yearling lambs; they must be without blemish for you. <margin>20</margin> And their grain offering shall be of fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths you shall prepare for a bull, and two-tenths [for the ram]...'"

# Chapter Thirty

<margin>1-2</margin> And Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the children of Israel, saying: “This is what the Lord has commanded. * If a man makes a vow to the Lord or takes an oath to bind himself with a pledge, he shall not break his word.
<margin>3</margin> According to all that proceeds from his mouth he shall do. * And if a woman makes a vow to the Lord
<margin>4</margin> and binds herself with a pledge in her father's house in her youth, * and her father hears her vow and the pledge with which she has bound herself, and her father says nothing to her, then all her vows shall stand. And every pledge with which
<margin>5</margin> she has bound herself shall stand. * But if her father forbids her on the day he hears it, none of her vows or her pledges
<margin>6</margin> with which she has bound herself shall stand. And the Lord will forgive her, because her father forbade her. * And if

## Chapter Thirty-Four

<margin>1-2</margin> And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: * Command the children of Israel and say to them: When you enter the land of Canaan <note>The "Promised Land," roughly corresponding to modern-day Israel, Palestine, and parts of Lebanon and Syria</note>, this is the land that shall fall to you as an inheritance—the land of Canaan according to its borders.
<margin>3</margin> * Your southern side shall be from the Wilderness of Zin <note>A desert region south of the Dead Sea</note> along the border of Edom. Your southern border shall extend from the end of the Salt Sea <note>The Dead Sea</note> to the east.
<margin>4</margin> Your border shall turn from the south of the Ascent of Akrabbim <note>original: "aqbat aqrabim," meaning 'Scorpions' Pass'</note>, pass through Zin, and its end shall be south of Kadesh Barnea. It shall go on to Hazar Addar and pass through Azmon.
<margin>5</margin> * Then the border shall turn from Azmon to the Brook of Egypt <note>original: "wadi misr," likely the Wadi el-Arish</note>, and its end shall be at the Sea <note>The Mediterranean Sea</note>.
<margin>6</margin> * As for the western border, the Great Sea <note>The Mediterranean Sea</note> shall be your boundary; this shall be your western border.
<margin>7</margin> * And this shall be your northern border: from the Great Sea you shall mark out your line to Mount Hor <note>Not the same Mount Hor where Aaron died, but a peak in the north, possibly in the Lebanon range</note>.
<margin>8</margin> * From Mount Hor you shall mark your line to the Entrance of Hamath <note>A major mountain pass and historical Syrian city</note>, and the end of the border shall be at Zedad.
<margin>9</margin> * Then the border shall go to Ziphron, and its end shall be at Hazar Enan. This shall be your northern border.
<margin>10</margin> * And you shall mark out your eastern border from Hazar Enan to Shepham.
<margin>11</margin> * The border shall go down from Shepham to Riblah on the east side of Ain <note>meaning 'spring'</note>. Then the border shall go down and reach the eastern side of the Sea of Chinnereth <note>The Sea of Galilee</note>.
<margin>12</margin> * Then the border shall go down to the Jordan, and its end shall be at the Salt Sea. This shall be your land according to its borders all around.
<margin>13</margin> * Then Moses commanded the children of Israel, saying: This is the land you shall divide by lot, which the Lord commanded to give to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.

## Chapter Thirty-Six

<margin>1</margin> The heads of the fathers’ houses of the clan of the children of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh, of the clans of the

men from other <term>tribes</term> <note>original: *asbat*, the plural of *sibt*, referring to the twelve tribal divisions of Israel</note> of the children of Israel, then their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of our fathers 
<margin>4</margin> and added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry. So it will be taken from our allotted inheritance. * And when 
the <term>Jubilee</term> <note>original: *al-yubil*, a year of release occurring every fifty years when alienated land traditionally returned to its original owners</note> comes for the children of Israel, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they married, 
and their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of our ancestors' tribe."
<margin>5</margin> So Moses commanded the children of Israel according to the word of the Lord, saying: "The tribe of the descendants of Joseph speaks rightly. 
<margin>6</margin> * This is what the Lord has commanded concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying: They may marry whom they please,
<margin>7</margin> but they must marry only within a clan of their father’s tribe. * So no inheritance of the children of Israel 
shall pass from tribe to tribe, but every one of the children of Israel shall keep the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.
<margin>8</margin> * Every daughter who possesses an inheritance in any tribe of the children of Israel shall be the wife of someone from 
<margin>9</margin> a clan of her father’s tribe, so that every one of the children of Israel may possess the inheritance of his fathers. * No 
inheritance shall pass from one tribe to another tribe, but each of the tribes of the children of Israel shall keep 
its own inheritance."
<margin>10</margin> Just as the Lord commanded Moses, so did the daughters of Zelophehad. * For Mahlah, Tirzah, 
<margin>11</margin> Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah—the daughters of Zelophehad—were married to the sons of their uncles. <note>In this context, marrying "sons of uncles" (cousins) ensured the land stayed within the specific family line of Manasseh.</note> * They married into the clans 
of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and so their inheritance remained in the tribe of their father's clan.

١ Observe the month of Abib <term>Abib: The first month of the ancient Hebrew calendar, occurring in the spring; later known as Nisan.</term> and perform a Passover for the Lord your God, because in the month of Abib the Lord

## Chapter Twenty-Two

<margin>1</margin> You shall not see your brother’s ox or his sheep wandering and ignore them; you must certainly return them to your brother. <margin>2</margin> * And if your brother is not near you, or if you do not know him, then you shall bring it into your house, and it shall remain <margin>3</margin> with you until your brother seeks it, then you shall return it to him. * You shall do the same with his donkey, and you shall do the same with his clothing. You shall do the same with every lost thing of your brother’s which he has lost and you have found. It is not permitted for you <margin>4</margin> to ignore it. * You shall not see your brother’s donkey or his ox fallen on the road and disregard them, but you must certainly help him lift them up.

<margin>5</margin> A woman shall not wear a man’s articles, nor shall a man put on a woman’s garment, for whoever does these things is an abomination to the Lord your God. <note>This law likely served to distinguish Israelite customs from certain pagan rituals involving cross-dressing.</note>

<margin>6</margin> If you happen upon a bird’s nest along the road, in any tree or on the ground, with <margin>7</margin> chicks or eggs, and the mother is sitting on the chicks or the eggs, you shall not take the mother with the young. * You shall surely let the mother go, but the young you may take for yourself, that it may go well with you and that you may prolong your days. <note>This is one of the few laws in the text that explicitly promises the reward of a long life for an act of compassion toward nature.</note>
<margin>8</margin> When you build a new house, you shall make a parapet for your roof, <note>original: "حائطًا لسطحك" (a wall for your roof). In the ancient Near East, flat roofs were used as living spaces; a low wall was a required safety feature.</note> so that you do not bring bloodguilt upon your house if anyone should fall from it.

<margin>9</margin> You shall not sow your field with two kinds of seed, lest the entire harvest—the seed you have sown and the yield of the <margin>10</margin> field—be forfeited. * You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together. <margin>11</margin> * You shall not wear a garment of mixed fabrics, wool and linen together.
<margin>12</margin> You shall make for yourself tassels on the four corners of your garment with which you cover yourself.
<margin>13</margin> <margin>14</margin> If a man takes a wife and, after he has gone in to her, he hates her * and charges her with shameful conduct and brings a bad name upon her, saying, “I took this woman, but when I approached her, I did not find <margin>15</margin> her a virgin,” * then the girl’s father and her mother shall take and bring the evidence of the girl's virginity to the elders of the city <margin>16</margin> at the gate. <note>The city gate was the traditional location for legal proceedings and public witness.</note> * And the girl’s father shall say to the elders, “I gave my daughter to this man as a wife, but he hated her, <margin>17</margin> * and look, he has charged her with shameful conduct, saying, ‘I did not find your daughter a virgin,’ yet this is the evidence of my daughter's virginity.”

## Chapter Twenty-Four

**1** If a man takes a woman and marries her, and she finds no favor in his eyes because he found in her some **indecent thing** <note>original: "عيب شيءٍ" ('ayba shay'in); literally "a defect of a thing," a phrase historically debated by scholars regarding the grounds for divorce</note>, and he writes her a **certificate of divorce**, puts it in her hand, and sends her out of his house. **2** And when she has departed from his house, she goes and becomes the wife of another man. **3** If the latter husband detests her and writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand, and sends her out of his house, or if the latter husband who took her as his wife dies, **4** her former husband who sent her away is not permitted to take her back again to be his wife after she has been defiled; for that is an **abomination** before the Lord. You shall not bring sin upon the land which the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance.

**5** When a man takes a **new wife**, he shall not go out with the army, nor shall any public duty be imposed upon him. He shall be free at home for one year to bring joy to the wife he has taken.

**6** No one shall take a **millstone** <note>original: "رحى" (raha); used for grinding grain into flour</note> or even its upper stone as a <term>pledge</term> <note>original: "رهناً" (rahnan); collateral for a debt</note>, for that would be taking a person's very life as security.

**7** If a man is found kidnapping any of his brothers, the children of Israel, and treats him as a slave or sells him, then that **thief shall die**; thus you shall purge the evil from among you.

**8** Take care in an outbreak of <term>leprosy</term> <note>original: "البرص" (al-baras); in the biblical context, this refers to various infectious skin diseases (Tzaraat) requiring ritual quarantine</note> to be very diligent and act according to everything the **Levitical priests** teach you. As I have commanded them, so you shall be careful to do. **9** Remember what the Lord your God did to **Miriam** <note>A reference to Numbers 12, where Miriam was temporarily struck with leprosy after challenging Moses's authority</note> on the way when you came out of **Egypt**.

**10** When you make your neighbor a loan of any kind, you shall not enter his house to seize his pledge. **11** * You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you are lending shall bring the pledge out to you.

## Chapter Thirty-One

<margin>1-2</margin> Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel. * And he said to them: "I am today one hundred and twenty years old. <margin>4</margin> And the Lord will do to them as He did to <term>Sihon and Og</term> <note>Two powerful Amorite kings defeated by the Israelites, often cited as evidence of God's favor.</note>, the kings of the Amorites, whom He destroyed along with their land. *

<summary>Moses prepares Israel for his death by appointing Joshua as his successor and commanding the periodic public reading of the Law during the Feast of Tabernacles. # Joshua

---

## Chapter One

1 After the death of Moses the servant of the Lord, the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, Moses' <term>assistant</term> <note>original: "خادم" (khadim). While it can mean "servant," in this context, it refers to Joshua's role as Moses' trusted aide and apprentice.</note>,

2 saying: "Moses my servant is dead. Now therefore, arise, cross over this Jordan, you and all this

## Chapter Two

2 And it was told to the king of Jericho, saying: "Behold, two men from the children of Israel have come here tonight to spy out the land." *

3 So the king of Jericho sent to Rahab, saying: "Bring out the men who have come to you and entered your house, for they have come to spy out all the land." *

4 But the woman took the men and hid them. She said: "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from. *

<margin>25</margin> And Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, her father’s household, and all that belonged to her. She has lived in the midst of Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.
<margin>26</margin> And Joshua swore an oath at that time, saying, "Cursed before the Lord be the man who rises up and rebuilds this city, Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn shall he lay its foundation, and at the cost of his youngest shall he set up its gates."

## Chapter Twenty

<margin>1-2</margin> Then the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying: "Speak to the children of Israel, saying: 'Designate for yourselves the **Cities of Refuge**, as I spoke to you through Moses,
<margin>3</margin> so that a killer who strikes a person down unintentionally and without knowledge <note>original: "سهواً بغير علم" (sahwan bi-ghayri ‘ilm). This refers to accidental manslaughter where there was no prior intent or malice.</note> may flee there. They shall be a refuge for you from the **avenger of blood**. <note>The "avenger of blood" (Wali al-Dam) was the next-of-kin responsible for seeking justice for the deceased. These cities provided a legal sanctuary to prevent cycles of private vengeance.</note>
<margin>4</margin> He shall flee to one of these cities, stand at the entrance of the city gate, and state his case in the ears of the elders of that city. They shall take him into the city and give him a place to live among them.
<margin>5</margin> And if the avenger of blood pursues him, they shall not hand the killer over to him, because he struck his neighbor without prior knowledge and did not hate him beforehand.
<margin>6</margin> He shall live in that city until he stands before the congregation for judgment, and until the death of the **High Priest** <note>original: "الكاهن العظيم" (al-kahin al-ʿazim). The death of the High Priest acted as a symbolic and legal conclusion to the term of exile, granting the individual a full pardon to return home.</note> who is in office in those days. Then the killer may return to his own city and his own house, to the city from which he fled.'"
<margin>7</margin> So they set apart **Kedesh** in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, **Shechem** in the hill country of Ephraim, and **Kiriath-arba** (that is, **Hebron**) in the hill country of Judah.
<margin>8</margin> And beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho, they designated **Bezer** in the wilderness on the plain from the tribe of Reuben, **Ramoth** in Gilead from the tribe of Gad, and **Golan** in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh.
<margin>9</margin> These were the designated cities for all the children of Israel and for the stranger residing among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally might flee there and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood until he stands before the congregation.

## Chapter Twenty-One

<margin>1</margin> Then the heads of the fathers' houses of the **Levites** approached **Eleazar the priest**, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers' houses of the tribes of the children of Israel.
<margin>2</margin> They spoke to them at **Shiloh** in the land of Canaan, saying: "The Lord commanded through Moses that we be given cities to live in, with their pasture lands for our livestock." <note>original: "مسارحها" (masarihiha). These were the commons or open suburban fields surrounding the city walls where the Levites could graze their herds.</note>
<margin>3</margin> So the children of Israel gave the Levites these cities and their pasture lands from their own inheritance, according to the word of the Lord.

### Chapter Two

1 And the Angel of the Lord came up from Gilgal to Bochim and said: "I led you up from Egypt and brought you to the land that I swore to your fathers, and I said, 'I will never break my covenant with you
2 forever.' And as for you, you shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land; you shall tear down their altars.

12 And they forsook the Lord God of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt; and they followed other gods from among the gods of the people who were all around them, and they bowed down to them, and they provoked the Lord to anger.
13 They forsook the Lord and served **Baal** and **Ashtaroth** <note>Ashtaroth is the plural of Ashtoreth (Astarte), the Phoenician goddess of love and war, often associated with Baal.</note>.
14 And the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel. So He delivered them into the hands of plunderers who despoiled them; and He sold them into the hands of their enemies all around, so that they could no longer stand before their enemies.
15 Wherever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for calamity, as the Lord had said, and as the Lord had sworn to them. And they were greatly distressed.

# Chapter Fifteen

<margin>1</margin> After some time, during the days of the wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife with a young goat. He said, "I will go into my wife’s chamber." But her father would not let him enter. 
<margin>2</margin> Her father said, "I truly thought that you utterly hated her, so I gave her to your companion. Is not her younger sister better than she? Let her be yours instead of her." 
<margin>3</margin> Samson said to them, "This time I shall be blameless regarding the Philistines if I do them harm." 
<margin>4</margin> So Samson went and caught three hundred jackals <note>original: "ابن آوى" — while often translated as "foxes" in some English Bibles, the Arabic term specifically refers to jackals, which were common in the region and more likely to be found in large groups.</note> and took torches. He turned them tail to tail and put a torch between each pair of tails in the middle. 
<margin>5</margin> Then he set the torches on fire and released them into the standing grain of the Philistines, burning the stacks, the standing grain, the vineyards, and the olive groves. 
<margin>6</margin> The Philistines asked, "Who has done this?" They were told, "Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he took his wife and gave her to his companion." So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father with fire. 
<margin>7</margin> Samson said to them, "Even if you do this, I will surely take revenge on you, and only after that will I stop." 
<margin>8</margin> And he struck them hip and thigh <note>An idiom meaning a total and ruthless slaughter.</note> with a great blow. Then he went down and stayed in the cleft of the rock of Etam.
<margin>9</margin> Then the Philistines went up and encamped in Judah and spread out through Lehi <note>Lehi means "jawbone," foreshadowing the weapon Samson will use in the following verses.</note>. 
<margin>10</margin> The men of Judah said, "Why have you come up against us?" They replied, "We have come up to bind Samson, to do to him as he did to us." 
<margin>11</margin> Then three thousand men of Judah went down to the cleft of the rock of Etam and said to Samson, "Do you not know that the Philistines rule over us? What is this that you have done to us?" He said to them, "As they did to me, so I have done to them."

## Chapter Seventeen

<margin>1 2</margin> There was a man from the hill country of Ephraim whose name was Micah. And he said to his mother, "The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from you, and about which you uttered a curse and also spoke in my ears—behold, the silver is with me; I took it." Then his mother said, "Blessed be you by the Lord, my son!" <margin>3</margin> So he returned the eleven hundred shekels of silver to his mother. Then his mother said, "I have truly dedicated the silver to the Lord from my hand for my son, to make a carved image and a cast image. So now, I return it to you." <margin>4</margin> Then he returned the silver to his mother. So his mother took two hundred shekels of silver and gave them to the silversmith, who made it into a carved image and a cast image; and they were in the house of Micah. <margin>5</margin> And the man Micah had a house of gods, and he made an ephod and <term>teraphim</term> <note>original: "ترافيم" — small household idols or cultic objects used in ancient Near Eastern divination.</note> and <insert>consecrated</insert> <note>original: "ملأ يد" — literally "filled the hand," a Hebrew idiom for ordaining or installing someone into a priestly office.</note> one of his sons, who became his priest. <margin>6</margin> In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.

<margin>1</margin> There was a certain man from **Ramathaim-zophim** <note>Meaning "The two heights of the Zophites," a town located in the hill country of Ephraim</note>, of the mountains of Ephraim, whose name was Elkanah the son of Jeroham, the son of

<margin>4</margin> And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests of the Lord there. * When the time came for Elkanah to sacrifice, 
<margin>5</margin> he would give portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and daughters. * But to Hannah he gave a double portion, because he loved Hannah, though the Lord had closed her womb. 
<margin>6</margin> * And her rival used to provoke her severely to make her miserable, because the Lord had closed her womb. 
<margin>7</margin> * This happened year after year; whenever she went up to the house of the Lord, her rival provoked her so much that she wept and 
<margin>8</margin> would not eat. * Then Elkanah her husband said to her, "Hannah, why do you weep? Why do you not eat? And why is your heart grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?"
<margin>9</margin> So Hannah rose after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh. Now Eli the priest was sitting 
<margin>10</margin> on his chair by the doorpost of the temple of the Lord. * And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed to the Lord 
<margin>11</margin> and wept in anguish. * Then she made a vow and said, "O Lord of Hosts, if You will indeed look on the affliction of Your maidservant and remember me, and not forget Your maidservant, but will give Your maidservant a male child, then I will give him to the Lord all the days of his life, and no **razor** <note>original: "موسى" (mūsā) - this refers to the Nazirite vow of dedication to God, similar to the vow taken by Samson</note> shall come upon his head." 
<margin>12</margin> * And it happened, as she continued praying before the Lord, 
<margin>13</margin> that Eli watched her mouth. * Hannah was speaking in her heart; only her lips moved, but her 
<margin>14</margin> voice was not heard. Therefore Eli thought she was drunk. * Eli said to her, "How long will you be drunk? 
<margin>15</margin> Put away your wine from you!" * But Hannah answered and said, "No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful 
<margin>16</margin> spirit. I have drunk neither wine nor intoxicating drink, but have poured out my soul before the Lord. * Do not consider your maidservant a **daughter of Belial** <term>daughter of Belial: a biblical idiom for a wicked, worthless, or lawless person</term>, for out of the abundance of my complaint and grief I have spoken until now."

<margin>33</margin> not be an old man in your house forever. * And any man of yours whom I do not cut off from my altar shall be to consume 
<margin>34</margin> your eyes and to grieve your soul. And all the descendants of your house shall die as young men. * And this shall be a 
<margin>35</margin> sign to you that shall come upon your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they shall both die. * And I will raise up for myself a faithful priest who shall do according to what is in my heart and in my soul. I will build him a sure house, 
<margin>36</margin> and he shall walk before my **anointed** <note>original: "مسيحي" (masīḥī); referring here to the future kings of Israel</note> forever. * And it shall come to pass that everyone who remains in your house will come to bow down to him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and say: "Please put me into one of the priestly offices, that I may eat a piece of bread."'"

### Chapter Thirteen

<margin>1-2</margin> Saul was one year old <note>original: "ibn sana," literally "son of a year." <margin>5</margin> The Philistines also gathered to fight against Israel: thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen, and people as numerous as the sand on the seashore. <margin>8</margin> He waited seven days, according to the time set by Samuel, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal; and the people were scattering from him. <margin>9</margin> So Saul said, "Bring the burnt offering and the peace offerings to me." So I forced myself <note>original: "tajalladtu," meaning he constrained himself or acted with a forced courage</note> and offered the burnt offering." <margin>13</margin> Samuel said to Saul, "You have acted foolishly. <margin>35</margin> In the morning, Jonathan went out into the field at the time appointed with David, and a small boy was with him. <margin>36</margin> He said to his boy, "Run, find the arrows which I shoot." As the boy ran, he shot an arrow beyond him. <margin>37</margin> When the boy came to the place where the arrow that Jonathan had shot lay, Jonathan called out after the boy and said, "Is the arrow not beyond you?" <margin>38</margin> And Jonathan called out after the boy, saying, "Hurry! Make haste! Do not stay!" Jonathan’s boy gathered up the arrow and came to his master. <margin>39</margin> But the boy knew nothing; only Jonathan and David knew the matter. <margin>40</margin> Then Jonathan gave his weapons to his boy and said to him, "Go, carry them into the city."

<margin>41</margin> As soon as the boy had gone, David rose from the south side, fell on his face to the ground, and bowed down three times. They kissed one another and wept with one another, until David’s grief exceeded Jonathan's. <margin>42</margin> Jonathan said to David, "Go in peace, for we have both sworn in the name of the Lord, saying, 'The Lord shall be between me and you, and between my offspring and your offspring forever.'" So David rose and departed, and Jonathan went into the city.

<summary>This page describes King Saul's violent outburst against Jonathan for defending David, leading to the final signal in the field where Jonathan warns David to flee. The chapter ends with a tearful farewell between the two friends as they reaffirm their eternal covenant before David goes into exile.</summary>

1 Now the Philistines <term>Philistines: A seafaring people who settled on the southern coast of Canaan and were the primary rivals of the early Israelites.</term> fought against Israel; the men of Israel fled before the Philistines 2 and fell slain on Mount Gilboa. <margin>28</margin> Afterward, when David heard of it, he said, “I and my kingdom are innocent before the Lord forever of the blood of Abner the son of Ner. <margin>29</margin> Let it fall on the head of Joab and on all his father’s house; and let there never fail to be in the house of Joab one who has a discharge, or is a leper, or who leans on a staff <note>Indicating physical infirmity or blindness.</note>, or who falls by the sword, or who lacks bread.” <margin>30</margin> So Joab and Abishai his brother killed Abner, because he had killed their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.

<margin>31</margin> Then David said to Joab and to all the people who were with him, “Tear your clothes, gird yourselves with sackcloth <note>A coarse fabric worn as a sign of mourning or repentance.</note>, and mourn before Abner.” And King David himself walked behind the bier <note>The stand on which a corpse or coffin is placed.</note>. <margin>32</margin> They buried Abner in Hebron; and the king lifted up his voice and wept at the grave of Abner, and all the people wept.

->### CHAPTER FOUR<-

<margin>1</margin> When the son of Saul <note>Ish-bosheth, who was reigning over the northern tribes.</note> heard that Abner had died in Hebron, his hands grew weak, and all Israel was dismayed. <margin>2</margin> Now the son of Saul had two men who were captains of raiding bands: the name of one was Baanah and the name of the other was Rechab, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the tribe of Benjamin. For Beeroth was also counted as part of Benjamin. <margin>3</margin> The Beerothites had fled to Gittaim and have lived there as foreigners until this day.

<margin>4</margin> And Jonathan, the son of Saul, had a son whose feet were crippled. He was five years old when the news of Saul and Jonathan’s deaths came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled, but as she was hurrying to escape, he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.

<margin>5</margin> The sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, set out and arrived at the house of Ish-bosheth during the heat of the day, while he was taking his noonday nap. <margin>6</margin> They entered the middle of the house as if to take wheat, and they stabbed him in the stomach. Then Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped. <margin>7</margin> When they had entered the house, he was lying on his bed in his bedroom; they struck him, killed him, and cut off his head. They took his head and traveled by way of the Arabah <note>The desert valley extending from the Sea of Galilee to the Dead Sea.</note> all night long.

<margin>8</margin> They brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David at Hebron and said to the king, "Behold, the head of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, your enemy who sought your life. The Lord has given my lord the king vengeance this day upon Saul and his descendants."

<margin>9</margin> But David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, "As the Lord lives, who has redeemed my soul from every distress, <margin>10</margin> when one told me, saying, 'Behold, Saul is dead,' and he thought himself a bringer of good news, I seized him and killed him in Ziklag. That was the reward I gave him for his news! <margin>11</margin> How much more, then, when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his own house upon his bed? Shall I not now require his blood from your hands..."

## Chapter Twelve

1 So the Lord sent Nathan <note>A prophet and close advisor to King David.</note> to David. He came to him and said, "There were two men in one
2 city; one was rich and the other was poor. * The rich man had very many sheep and cattle.
3 * But the poor man had nothing except one small ewe lamb which he had bought and raised;
it grew up with him and with all his children. It ate from his morsel, drank from his cup, and slept in 
his bosom; it was like a daughter to him. * A traveler came to the rich man, and he was unwilling to take from 
his own sheep or cattle to prepare a meal for the guest who had come to him. Instead, he took the poor man's lamb and prepared
it for the man who had come to him." * Then David’s anger burned greatly against the man, and he said to Nathan,
5 "As the Lord lives, the man who has done this deserves to die!
6 * And he must restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing and because he showed no pity."
7 Then Nathan said to David, "You are the man! Thus says the Lord, God of Israel: 'I 
anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul. * I gave you 
8 your master’s house and your master’s wives into your keeping; I gave you the house of Israel and Judah. And if 
9 that had been too little, I would have added much more to you. * Why have you despised the word of the Lord,
doing evil in His sight? You have struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword and taken his wife to be 
your wife; you killed him with the sword of the <term>Ammonites<note>original: "بني عمون" (Bani 'Ammon). An ancient Semitic-speaking people often at war with the Israelites.</note></term>. * Now therefore, the sword shall never depart from your house, 
10 because you have despised Me and taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.' * Thus 
11 says the Lord: 'Behold, I will raise up evil against you from your own house; I will take your wives before 
your very eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he shall lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.
12 * For you did it secretly, but I will do this thing before all Israel and before the 
13 sun.'" * So David said to Nathan, "I have sinned against the Lord." And Nathan said to David, 
14 "The Lord also has put away your sin; you shall not die. * However, because by this deed you have 
15 given the enemies of the Lord cause to <term>scoff<note>original: "يشمتون" (yashmatun). To feel malicious joy or mock at another's misfortune or failure.</note></term>, the child who is born to you shall surely die." * Then Nathan 
went to his house.

<margin>30</margin> While they were on the way, the news reached David, saying, "Absalom has killed all the king’s sons, and not one of them is left!"

10 David’s heart struck him with guilt after he had counted the people. David said to the Lord, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done. And now, O Lord, I pray You, take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly." 
11 When David rose in the morning, the word of the Lord came to Gad the prophet, David’s seer <note>A 'seer' was a specific type of prophet who received divine revelations through visions</note>, saying: 
12 "Go and tell David, 'Thus says the Lord: Three things I offer you; choose one of them for yourself, that I may do it to you.'" 
13 So Gad came to David and told him, and said to him, "Shall seven years of famine come to you in your land? Or will you flee three months before your enemies while they pursue you? Or shall there be three days of plague in your land? Now consider and see what answer I should return to Him who sent me." 
14 David said to Gad, "I am in great distress. Let us fall into the hand of the Lord, for His mercies are great; but do not let me fall into the hand of man." 
15 So the Lord sent a plague upon Israel from the morning until the appointed time. From Dan to Beersheba <note>original: "من دان الى بئرسبع" - an idiom for the entire extent of the kingdom from north to south</note>, seventy thousand men of the people died. 
16 And when the angel stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, the Lord relented from the destruction and said to the angel who was destroying the people, "It is enough; now stay your hand." And the angel of the Lord was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite <note>The Jebusites were the original inhabitants of Jerusalem; this threshing floor is traditionally identified as the site where Solomon’s Temple would later be built</note>. 
17 When David saw the angel who was striking the people, he spoke to the Lord and said, "Look, I have sinned, and I have done wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? Let Your hand, I pray, be against me and against my father’s house."

18 And Gad came that day to David and said to him, "Go up, erect an altar to the Lord on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite." 
19 So David went up according to the word of Gad, as the Lord commanded. 
20 Araunah looked and saw the king and his servants coming toward him. So Araunah went out and bowed down before the king with his face to the ground. 
21 Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" David said, "To buy the threshing floor from you, in order to build an altar to the Lord, so that the plague may be withdrawn from the people." 
22 Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take and offer up what seems good in his eyes. Look, here are the oxen for the burnt sacrifice, and threshing sledges <note>Heavy wooden frames with blades underneath used to separate grain from husks</note> and the tools of the oxen for wood." 
23 All these things Araunah, the king <note>original: "ارونة الملك" - some scholars suggest Araunah may have been the former Jebusite king of Jerusalem before David's conquest</note>, gave to the king. And Araunah said to the king, "May the Lord your God accept you." 
24 But the king said to Araunah, "No, but I will surely buy it from you for a price; I will not offer burnt offerings to the Lord my God [that cost me nothing]..."

## 1 Kings

### Chapter One

1 Now King David was old, advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he could not keep warm.
2 Therefore his servants said to him, "Let a young virgin be sought for our lord the king, and let her stand before the king and be his caregiver; let her lie in your bosom, that our lord the king may be warm."
3 So they searched for a beautiful young woman throughout all the borders of Israel, and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
4 The young woman was very beautiful; she became the king's caregiver and served him, but the king did not know her <note>A biblical idiom meaning they did not have intimate relations.</note>.

5 Then Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, "I will be king." And he prepared for himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
6 His father [David] had never displeased him at any time by saying, "Why have you done so?" He was also a very handsome man, and his mother bore him after Absalom.
7 He conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they followed and helped Adonijah.
8 But Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and the mighty men who belonged to David were not with Adonijah.
