## Chapter Five

<margin>1</margin> But concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need that I should write to you,
<margin>2</margin> for you yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night.
<margin>3</margin> For when they say, "Peace and safety!" then sudden destruction comes upon them, like <term>labor pains</term> <note>original: "المخاض" (al-makhād), the specific pain of childbirth used here to describe the inevitability and suddenness of judgment</note> upon a pregnant woman,
<margin>4</margin> and they shall not escape. * But you, brothers, are not in darkness, that this day should overtake you
<margin>5-6</margin> as a thief. * You are all sons of light and sons of the day. We are not of the night nor of darkness. * Therefore let us not sleep,
<margin>7</margin> as others do, but let us watch and be sober. * For those who sleep, sleep at night, and those who get drunk
<margin>8</margin> are drunk at night. * But let us who are of the day be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith
<margin>9</margin> and love, and as a helmet the hope of salvation. * For God did not appoint us to wrath, but to obtain
<margin>10</margin> salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ, * who died for us, that whether we wake or sleep,
<margin>11</margin> we should live together with Him. * Therefore comfort each other and edify one another, just as you also are doing.
<margin>12</margin> And we ask you, brothers, to recognize those who labor among you, and are over you in the Lord
<margin>13</margin> and admonish you, * and to esteem them very highly in love for their work's sake. Be at peace
<margin>14</margin> among yourselves. * Now we exhort you, brothers, warn those who are <term>unruly</term> <note>original: "بلا ترتيب" (bilā tartīb), meaning those who live without order or discipline</note>. Encourage the <term>faint-hearted</term> <note>original: "صغار النفوس" (sighār al-nufūs), literally 'those with small souls,' referring to the discouraged or timid</note>.
<margin>15</margin> Help the weak. Be patient with all. * See that no one renders evil for evil to anyone, but always pursue what is good both for yourselves and for all.
<margin>16, 17-18</margin> * Rejoice always. * Pray without ceasing. * In everything give thanks; for this is the
<margin>19</margin> will of God in Christ Jesus for you. * Do not quench the Spirit. * Do not despise
<margin>21, 22</margin> prophecies. * Test all things; hold fast what is good. * Abstain from every form of evil.

## Chapter Three

<margin>1</margin> Finally, brothers, pray for us that the word of the Lord may spread rapidly and be glorified, just as it has been among 
<margin>2</margin> you, * and that we may be delivered from wicked and evil men; for faith does not belong to everyone.
<margin>3 4-20</margin> But the Lord is faithful, who will establish you and guard you from the evil one. * And we have confidence in the Lord 
<margin>5</margin> concerning you, that you are doing what we command you and will continue to do so. * May the Lord guide your hearts into the love of God and into the patience of Christ.
<margin>6</margin> But we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you keep away from every brother who walks 
<margin>7</margin> in <term>disorder</term> <note>original: "بلا ترتيب" (bla tartib); literally "without order," referring to those who were idle or neglected the community's rules of conduct.</note> and not according to the teaching which he received from us. * For you yourselves know how 
<margin>8</margin> you ought to imitate us, for we were not disorderly among you, * nor did we eat anyone’s bread for free; instead, we were working with labor and toil night and day so that we would not be a burden to 
<margin>9</margin> any of you. * This was not because we do not have authority, but to offer ourselves as a model so that 
<margin>10</margin> you might imitate us. * For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: if anyone 
<margin>11</margin> does not want to work, let him not eat either. * For we hear that some walk among you in 
<margin>12</margin> disorder, doing no work at all, but are busybodies. * Now such persons we command and exhort by our Lord Jesus Christ that they work quietly and eat their own bread. * As for you, 
<margin>13 14</margin> brothers, do not lose heart in doing good. * And if anyone does not obey our word in this letter, 
<margin>15</margin> <term>note that person</term> <note>original: "سموا هذا" (summu hadha); to mark or identify someone for the purpose of community discipline.</note> and do not associate with him, so that he may be ashamed. * Yet do not count him as an enemy, but warn him 
<margin>16</margin> as a brother. * Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace always in every way. The Lord be with all of you.
<margin>17</margin> This greeting is in my own hand—Paul’s—which is a sign in every letter; this is how I write.
<margin>18</margin> * The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. (Amen)

13 I who was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor, and an insolent man. But I was shown mercy because I acted

16 Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the first. * But for this reason I was shown mercy

### Chapter Three

<margin>1-2</margin> Trustworthy is the saying: if anyone aspires to the <term>episcopacy</term> <note>original: "الاسقفية" (al-usqufiyya); referring to the office of a bishop, overseer, or superintendent within the early church.</note>, he desires a noble task. * Therefore, a bishop must be blameless, the husband of one wife, sober-minded, sensible, respectable, hospitable to strangers, 
<margin>3</margin> and able to teach; * not addicted to wine, not violent, nor greedy for <term>dishonorable gain</term> <note>original: "الربح القبيح" (al-ribh al-qabih); literally "ugly profit," usually translated as "filthy lucre" in older English versions.</note>, but gentle,

<margin>6-7</margin> * He must not be a <term>recent convert</term> <note>original: "حديث الايمان" (hadith al-iman); literally "new in faith," a novice.</note>, lest he become conceited and fall into the condemnation of the devil. * Moreover, he must have a good reputation among those on the outside, so that he may not fall into disgrace and the snare of the devil.
<margin>8</margin> Likewise, <term>deacons</term> <note>original: "الشمامسة" (al-shamamisa); from the Greek 'diakonos,' meaning those who serve or minister to the needs of the community.</note> must be dignified, not double-tongued, not addicted 
<margin>9</margin> to much wine, nor greedy for dishonorable gain. * They must hold the mystery of the faith with a pure conscience. * And

<margin>12</margin> women must be dignified, not slanderers, but sober and faithful in all things. * Let 
<margin>13</margin> deacons each be the husband of one wife, managing their children and their own households well. * For those who serve well as deacons gain a good standing for themselves and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
<margin>14</margin> I am writing these things to you, hoping to come to you soon. * But if I 
<margin>15</margin> am delayed, you will know how one ought to conduct oneself in the house of God, which is the church of the 
<margin>16</margin> living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth. * By common confession, great is the <term>mystery of godliness</term> <note>original: "سرّ التقوى" (sirr al-taqwa); referring to the core revealed truths of the Christian faith regarding the nature of Christ.</note>: God was revealed in the flesh, vindicated in the Spirit, seen by angels, preached among the nations, believed on in the world, and taken up in glory.

# The Epistle of Paul the Apostle to Titus

## Chapter One

1 Paul, a servant <note>original: "عبد" (*‘abd*); traditionally "slave" or "bondservant," a title of humble service to God.</note> of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, for the sake of the faith of God’s chosen ones and the knowledge
2 of the truth which is according to godliness * in the hope of eternal life which 
3 God, who cannot lie, promised before the eternal ages * and has manifested His word in its proper 
4 times through the preaching with which I have been entrusted according to the command of God our Savior * To Titus, my true son <note>original: "الابن الصريح" (*al-ibn al-ṣarīḥ*); "true" or "genuine" son, indicating Titus's spiritual lineage through Paul’s teaching.</note> according to our common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Savior.
5 For this reason, I left you in Crete <note>A large island in the Mediterranean where Paul had previously traveled.</note> that you might set in order the things that are lacking 
6 and appoint elders in every city as I commanded you * if anyone is blameless, the husband of 
7 one wife, having faithful children not accused of dissipation <note>original: "الخلاعة" (*al-khalā‘a*); refers to reckless or riotous living.</note> or rebellion * For a bishop <term>bishop: "الاسقف" (al-usquf); meaning an overseer or guardian of the church</term> must be blameless as a steward of God, not self-willed, not quick-tempered, not a 
8 drunkard, not violent, nor greedy for dishonest gain * but hospitable to strangers, a lover of good, 
9 sober-minded, just, holy, self-controlled * holding fast to the faithful word which is according to the teaching, 
10 so that he may be able to exhort with sound doctrine and to convict those who contradict it * For there are 
many rebellious people, empty talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision <note>referring to Jewish converts who insisted on the necessity of following Mosaic Law, such as circumcision, for salvation.</note>,
11 whose mouths must be stopped, for they subvert whole houses, teaching what they ought 
12 not, for the sake of dishonest gain * One of them, a prophet of their own, said: "The Cretans 
13 are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons" <note>This is a famous quote by the Cretan poet and philosopher Epimenides, often called the "Cretan Paradox."</note> * This testimony is true. For this reason, 
14 rebuke them sharply so that they may be sound in the faith * not paying attention to Jewish myths 
15 and the commandments of men who turn away from the truth * To the pure, all things are pure; but to those who are defiled...

# The Letter to Philemon

<margin>4-5</margin> I thank my God always, mentioning you in my prayers, hearing of your love and the faith which you have toward the Lord Jesus and for all the saints, <margin>6</margin> so that the sharing of your faith may become effective in the knowledge of every good thing that is in you for the sake of Christ Jesus. <margin>7</margin> For we have great joy and comfort because of your love, for the hearts <note>original: "احشاء" (*ahshā’*); literally "bowels" or "entrails," used in the ancient world to refer to the seat of deep emotions and the core of one's being.</note> of the saints have been refreshed through you, O brother.

<margin>8-9</margin> Therefore, although I have much confidence in Christ to command you to do what is proper, I rather appeal to you for love’s sake—being such a person as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ. <margin>10</margin> I appeal to you for my son Onesimus <note>The name Onesimus means "profitable" or "useful" in Greek, which leads to Paul's wordplay in the following verse.</note>, whom I have begotten while in my chains. <margin>11</margin> He was formerly useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me. <margin>12</margin> I have sent him back; receive him, therefore, as my very heart <note>literally "my bowels" (*ahshā’*), indicating deep affection.</note>. <margin>13</margin> I wished to keep him with me so that he might serve me on your behalf in the chains of the gospel, <margin>14</margin> but I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your goodness might not be out of necessity, but of your own free will.

<margin>15</margin> For perhaps for this reason he was separated from you for a short time, that you might have him back forever— <margin>16</margin> no longer as a slave, but better than a slave: as a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord. <margin>17</margin> If then you count me a partner, receive him as you would receive me. <margin>18</margin> And if he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, put that on my account. <margin>19</margin> I, Paul, am writing this with my own hand: I will repay it—not to mention that you owe me even your own self. <margin>20</margin> Yes, brother, let me have joy from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in the Lord.

<margin>21</margin> Having confidence in your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say. <margin>22</margin> At the same time, prepare a lodging for me, for I hope that through your prayers I shall be granted to you. <margin>23</margin> Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you, <margin>24</margin> as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers. <margin>25</margin> The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

# Chapter Two

<margin>1-2</margin>
Therefore we must pay much closer attention to what we have heard, lest we drift away from it. For if the word spoken through angels <note>In Jewish tradition, the Law of Moses was often described as being delivered by angels.</note> proved steadfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just penalty,
<margin>3</margin>

<margin>9</margin>

<margin>10</margin>

<margin>13</margin>

## Chapter Twelve

١ Therefore, since we also have such a great cloud of witnesses <note>The "cloud of witnesses" refers to the long list of faithful figures just mentioned in chapter 11, imagining them as spectators in an arena.</note> surrounding us, let us cast off every weight and the sin that so easily entangles us, and let us run with endurance the race

٨ discipline, God is treating you as sons. For what son is there whom his father does not discipline? * But if you are without

<margin>1</margin> James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, sends greetings to the twelve

of life, which the Lord has promised to those who love him.

## Chapter Three

١ Do not become many teachers, my brothers, knowing that we shall receive a greater judgment.  
٢ * For we all stumble in many things. If anyone does not stumble in speech, he is a perfect man, able to bridle his whole body as well.  
٣ * Behold, we put bits <note>original: اللجم (al-lujum) — the metal pieces of a bridle placed in a horse's mouth to control it</note> into the mouths of horses so that they obey us, and we guide their whole bodies.  
٤ * Look at ships as well; though they are so large and are driven by fierce winds, they are guided by a very small rudder wherever the pilot's <note>original: المدير (al-mudir) — literally "the director" or "the one in charge," referring here to the steersman or captain</note> intention wills.  
٥ * Even so, the tongue is a small member, yet it boasts of great things. Behold how great a forest <note>original: وقود (waqud) — literally "fuel" or "kindling," implying the material that a small flame can ignite into a blaze</note> a little fire burns!  
٦ * And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity. The tongue is so set among our members that it defiles the whole body, sets on fire the course of nature <note>original: دائرة الكون (da'irat al-kawn) — literally "the circle of the universe" or "cycle of existence"</note>, and is set on fire by hell <note>term: hell (Gehenna) — from the Arabic "jahannam," used here to denote the source of destructive speech</note>.  
٧ * For every nature of beasts, birds, reptiles, and sea creatures is tamed and has been tamed by human nature.  
٨ * But no human being can tame the tongue. It is an uncontrollable evil, full of deadly poison.  
٩ * With it we bless God the Father, and with it we curse people, who have been created in the likeness of God.  
١٠ * From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, it is not right for these things to be so.  
١١ * Does a spring send forth from the same opening <note>original: عين (ayn) — literally "eye," a common poetic term for a spring or well-head</note> both sweet and bitter water?  
١٢ * Can a fig tree, my brothers, produce olives, or a grapevine produce figs? Likewise, no spring can produce both salt water and sweet.  
١٣ * Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show his works by his good conduct in the meekness of wisdom.  
١٤ * But if you have bitter envy and selfish ambition <note>original: تحزّب (tahazzub) — refers to factionalism, partisanship, or the forming of biased groups</note> in your hearts, do not boast and lie against the truth.  
١٥ * This is not the wisdom descending from above, but it is earthly, sensual <note>term: sensual (soul-led) — translated from "nafsaniyya," referring to the lower human nature or "soulish" instincts as opposed to the spirit</note>, and demonic.  
١٦ * For where envy and selfish ambition exist, there is disorder and every evil matter.  
١٧ * But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, yielding, full of mercy and good fruits, without doubt or hypocrisy.  
١٨ * And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who  
->make peace.<-

### Chapter Four

<margin>١</margin> From where do wars and quarrels among you come? Are they not from here, from your pleasures that war <margin>٢ *</margin> in your members? * You desire and you do not possess. You murder and envy and are not able to obtain. <margin>٣</margin> You quarrel and fight, and you do not possess because you do not ask. * You ask and you do not receive because you ask wrongly <note>original: رديّاً (raddiyan) — poorly, wickedly, or with bad intent</note>, so that you may spend it on your pleasures. <margin>٤</margin> You adulterers and adulteresses, do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity toward God? Whoever, therefore, wants to <margin>٥</margin> be a friend of the world has become an enemy of God. * Or do you think that the Scripture says in vain: <margin>٦</margin> "The Spirit who dwells in us yearns to envy"? * But He gives a greater grace. Therefore <margin>٧</margin> it says: "God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble." * Therefore, submit to God. <margin>٨</margin> Resist the devil <note>term: devil — from the Arabic "iblis," the primary name for the adversary in this context</note> and he will flee from you. * Draw near to God and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, <margin>٩</margin> you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded <note>original: ذوي الرايين (dhawi al-ra'yayn) — literally "those of two opinions" or "wavering between two thoughts"</note>. * Be miserable and mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned <margin>١٠</margin> to mourning and your joy to gloom. * Humble yourselves before the Lord and He will lift you up. <margin>١١</margin> Do not speak evil of one another, brothers. He who speaks evil of a brother and judges his brother speaks evil of the law <note>term: the law — from the Arabic "al-namus," often used in Christian Arabic to refer to the revealed Law of God</note> and judges the law. And if you judge the law, you are not a doer <margin>١٢</margin> of the law but a judge of it. * There is one Lawgiver who is able to save and to destroy. But who are you to judge another?

<margin>١٣</margin> Come now, you who say, "Today or tomorrow we will go to this city or that <margin>١٤</margin> and spend one year there, and trade and make a profit," * you who do not know the matter of tomorrow. <margin>١٥</margin> For what is your life? It is a vapor <note>original: بخار (bukhar) — steam, mist, or vapor, used here as a metaphor for the fleeting nature of human existence</note> that appears for a little while and then vanishes. * Instead, you ought to say, <margin>١٦</margin> "If the Lord wills and we live, we will do this or that." * But now you boast in your <margin>١٧</margin> arrogance. All such boasting is evil. * Therefore, to him who knows to do what is good and does not do it, to him it is sin.

# The First Epistle of Peter the Apostle

## Chapter One

1 Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers <note>original: المتغربين (al-mutagharribīn) — meaning those living away from their homeland; exiles</note> of the dispersion <note>original: شتات (shatāt) — referring to the Diaspora, the scattering of believers across various regions</note> of Pontus, Galatia, 2 Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia <note>These were all Roman provinces located in what is now modern-day Turkey</note>, the chosen * according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in the sanctification of the Spirit, for obedience and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ. May grace and peace be multiplied to you.

3 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to His abundant mercy has begotten us 4 again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead * to an inheritance that is incorruptible, 5 undefiled, and does not fade away, reserved in heaven for you * who by the power of God 6 are guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time. * In this you 7 greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you are grieved by various trials * so that the testing of your faith—which is much more precious than gold that perishes, though it is tested by fire— 8 may be found to result in praise, honor, and glory at the revelation of Jesus Christ. * Whom, having not seen, you love. Though you do not see Him now, yet believing in Him, you rejoice with joy 9 unspeakable and full of glory * receiving the end of your faith, the salvation of your souls. * This salvation 11 the prophets have searched and inquired after, who prophesied of the grace that was intended for you * searching for what time or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ who was in them did signify when He 12 testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ and the glories that should follow. * To them it was revealed that, not for themselves but for us, they were ministering these things which have now been reported to you by those who have preached the gospel to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven—things which the angels desire to look into.

13 Therefore, gird up the loins of your mind <note>original: منطقوا احقاء ذهنكم (mantiqū ahqā’ dhihnikum) — an idiom meaning to prepare oneself mentally for action, similar to tucking in long robes before a journey</note>, be sober, and rest your hope fully upon the grace...

<meta>This page concludes the final chapter of the Revelation of John, continuing from the list of those excluded from the holy city and ending with the final benediction of the New Testament.</meta>

# Revelation of John * 22 *

<margin>15</margin> <unclear>...</unclear>ers, and everyone who loves and practices a lie. <note>This concludes the list from the previous page of those who are excluded from the New Jerusalem.</note>

<margin>16</margin> I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify to you these things in the churches. I am the <term>Root and Offspring of David</term><note>original: "أصل وذرية داود" (asl wa dhurriyat Dawud) — A title asserting that Jesus is the fulfillment of the royal lineage of King David.</note>, the bright <term>Morning Star</term><note>original: "كوكب الصبح المنير" (kawkab al-subh al-munir) — A metaphor for Christ as the herald of a new, eternal day.</note>.

<margin>17</margin> And the Spirit and the bride say: Come. And let him who hears say: Come. And let him who thirsts come; and whoever desires, let him take the <term>water of life</term><note>original: "ماء الحياة" (ma' al-hayah) — Representing the gift of eternal life, offered without cost to those who seek it.</note> freely.

<margin>18</margin> For I testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: If anyone adds to these things, God will add to him the plagues that are written in this book.

<margin>19</margin> And if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part from the <term>Book of Life</term><note>original: "سفر الحياة" (sifr al-hayah) — The heavenly record of those destined for salvation.</note>, and from the holy city, and from the things which are written in this book.

<margin>20</margin> He who testifies to these things says: "Yes, I am coming quickly." Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus!

<margin>21</margin> The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen. <note>The manuscript concludes with this traditional blessing, which serves as the final sentence of the Christian Bible.</note>

<summary>This final page of the Revelation of John concludes the New Testament with a personal testimony from Jesus, an invitation to receive eternal life, and a solemn warning against altering the prophecy.</summary>
<keywords>Revelation, New Jerusalem, Jesus Christ, Morning Star, Water of Life, Book of Life, prophecy, benediction</keywords>
